Outage Filename: ./20190823-Summary of the Amazon EC2 Issues in the Asia Pacific (Tokyo) Region (AP-NORTHEAST-1).txt
--
Based on the provided text, I will resume the outage for Amazon AWS.

**Outage Details:**

* **Cloud Provider:** Amazon AWS
* **Incident:** A small percentage of EC2 servers in a single Availability Zone (AZ) in the Tokyo (AP-NORTHEAST-1) Region shut down due to overheating.
* **Start Time:** 12:36 PM JST on August 23, 2019
* **Duration:** The outage lasted for approximately 3 hours and 45 minutes.

**Impacted Services and Regions/AZs:**

* Amazon EC2 in the Tokyo (AP-NORTHEAST-1) Region, specifically in a single Availability Zone.
* Amazon EBS resources in the affected area of the Availability Zone.
* Some other services, such as RDS, Redshift, ElastiCache, and Workspaces, would have seen some impact if their underlying EC2 instances were affected.

**Root Cause:**
The root cause of the outage was a control system failure that caused multiple, redundant cooling systems to fail in parts of the affected Availability Zone.

**Downtime Period:**

* The affected cooling systems were restored at 3:21 PM JST.
* Temperatures in the affected areas began to return to normal after the cooling systems were restored.
* Power was restored to the affected instances by 6:30 PM JST.
* A small number of instances and volumes hosted on hardware that was adversely affected by the loss of power and excessive heat took longer to recover.

**Resolved Time:** The outage was marked as resolved at 6:30 PM JST on August 23, 2019.

Based on the provided text, I will resume the outage for Microsoft Azure.

**Outage Details:**

* **Incident Duration:** The incident lasted for approximately 6 hours and 36 minutes.
* **Start Time:** The outage started at 21:30 UTC.
* **End Time:** The outage was resolved by 03:26 UTC on February 26, 2021.
* **Impacted Services:** Front-end services for other clusters in the region also made calls to the impacted cluster's front-end service to obtain configuration. These calls were timed out due to unavailability, triggering the same unhandled failure condition and resulting crash.

**Root Cause:**

The root cause of the outage was a code defect in a version update of a component that controls network traffic routing between Azure regions. The main parameters of the new code were invoked only at production scale and scope levels, which led to the prevention of anomaly detection from occurring. This resulted in an abnormal, sudden increase in the number of unhealthy devices and forced a health validation of those devices before removing routes from the network.

**Downtime Period:**

The downtime period was approximately 6 hours and 36 minutes.

**Resolution Time:**

The outage was marked as resolved by 03:26 UTC on February 26, 2021.

Affected Services and Features:
Google Cloud Composer
Regions/Zones:
Global

Description:
Google Cloud Composer users experienced an elevated failure rate when creating, resizing, or upgrading to newer versions of Cloud Composer 2 Environments with Private IP configuration. This was due to an inadvertent issue introduced by a recent change to the latest stable Container Operating System (COS) image used by Cloud Composer in one of its workloads.

Root Cause:
The root cause was due to an issue introduced by a recent change to the latest stable Container Operating System (COS) image used by Cloud Composer in one of its workloads.
The new version of the COS image (M113) moved from iptables-legacy to iptables-nft package as the default, which impacted Konlet (system executing containers)'s handling of iptables to break.

Downtime Period:
Affected environments with Private IP configuration that experienced upgrade failures during the incident will now upgrade successfully.
Fewer than 20 customer environments encountered upgrade failures and all of the customer environments with Private IP configuration that experienced upgrade failures during the incident will now upgrade successfully.

**Summary:**

Google Cloud Composer was impacted in Global regions, with a downtime period of affected environments with Private IP configuration. The root cause was an issue introduced by a recent change to the latest stable Container Operating System (COS) image used by Cloud Composer in one of its workloads.

**IBM Cloud Services Impacted**

* Hyper Protect DBaaS: Impacted customers experienced provisioning failures in Frankfurt, London, Tokyo, Sydney, US-East, and US-South regions.

**Private DNS Services Impacted**

* Private DNS resolution timeouts from IKS clusters in VPC in Frankfurt, London, Tokyo, Sydney, US-East, and US-South regions.
* Private hostname lookups for VSIs on VPC were not successful in Frankfurt, London, Tokyo, Sydney, US-East, and US-South regions.
* Any service that uses a Virtual Private Endpoint in VPC was unavailable in Frankfurt, London, Tokyo, Sydney, US-East, and US-South regions.

**Cloudant Services Impacted**

* Cloudant services returned to normal state on 26 May 2021 at 01:40 UTC after being restricted for 12 hours and 7 minutes.

**Root Cause of Outage**

The root cause of the outage was an abnormally high burst of Private DNS traffic that caused resource constraints in the Cloudant HA Proxy Load Balancers, leading to service impact due to congestion on these devices.

**Outage Timeline**

* 25 May 2021 13:33 UTC: Incident started
* 25 May 2021 14:20 UTC: Affected clusters were identified
* 25 May 2021 15:16 UTC: Disruptive traffic was identified
* 25 May 2021 15:51 UTC: Isolation and removal of Private DNS traffic allowed cluster traffic to restart in Sydney
* 25 May 2021 16:09 UTC: Service recovery in Sydney was confirmed and isolation of traffic continued for other clusters
* 26 May 2021 01:28 UTC: Rate-limited updates were rolled out across all affected regions
* 26 May 2021 01:40 UTC: Cloudant services returned to normal state

**Outage Summary**

The outage lasted for 12 hours and 7 minutes, starting on 25 May 2021 at 13:33 UTC. The root cause of the outage was an abnormally high burst of Private DNS traffic that caused resource constraints in the Cloudant HA Proxy Load Balancers.

Based on the provided text, I will resume the outage for Amazon AWS.

**Outage Details:**

* **Cloud Provider:** Amazon AWS
* **Incident:** A small percentage of EC2 servers in a single Availability Zone (AZ) in the Tokyo (AP-NORTHEAST-1) Region shut down due to overheating.
* **Start Time:** 12:36 PM JST on August 23, 2019
* **Duration:** The outage lasted for approximately 3 hours and 45 minutes.

**Impacted Services and Regions/AZs:**

* Amazon EC2 in the Tokyo (AP-NORTHEAST-1) Region, specifically in a single Availability Zone.
* Amazon EBS resources in the affected area of the Availability Zone.
* Some other services, such as RDS, Redshift, ElastiCache, and Workspaces, would have seen some impact if their underlying EC2 instances were affected.

**Root Cause:**
The root cause of the outage was a control system failure that caused multiple, redundant cooling systems to fail in parts of the affected Availability Zone.

**Downtime Period:**

* The affected cooling systems were restored at 3:21 PM JST.
* Temperatures in the affected areas began to return to normal after the cooling systems were restored.
* Power was restored to the affected instances by 6:30 PM JST.
* A small number of instances and volumes hosted on hardware that was adversely affected by the loss of power and excessive heat took longer to recover.

**Resolved Time:** The outage was marked as resolved at 6:30 PM JST on August 23, 2019.

Based on the provided text, I will resume the outage for Amazon AWS.

**Outage Details:**

* **Cloud Provider:** Amazon AWS
* **Incident:** A small percentage of EC2 servers in a single Availability Zone (AZ) in the Tokyo (AP-NORTHEAST-1) Region shut down due to overheating.
* **Start Time:** 12:36 PM JST on August 23, 2019
* **Duration:** The outage lasted for approximately 3 hours and 45 minutes.

**Impacted Services and Regions/AZs:**

* Amazon EC2 in the Tokyo (AP-NORTHEAST-1) Region, specifically in a single Availability Zone.
* Amazon EBS resources in the affected area of the Availability Zone.
* Some other services, such as RDS, Redshift, ElastiCache, and Workspaces, would have seen some impact if their underlying EC2 instances were affected.

**Root Cause:**
The root cause of the outage was a control system failure that caused multiple, redundant cooling systems to fail in parts of the affected Availability Zone.

**Downtime Period:**

* The affected cooling systems were restored at 3:21 PM JST.
* Temperatures in the affected areas began to return to normal after the cooling systems were restored.
* Power was restored to the affected instances by 6:30 PM JST.
* A small number of instances and volumes hosted on hardware that was adversely affected by the loss of power and excessive heat took longer to recover.

**Resolved Time:** The outage was marked as resolved at 6:30 PM JST on August 23, 2019.

Based on the provided text, I will resume the outage for Microsoft Azure.

**Outage Details:**

* **Incident Duration:** The incident lasted for approximately 6 hours and 36 minutes.
* **Start Time:** The outage started at 21:30 UTC.
* **End Time:** The outage was resolved by 03:26 UTC on February 26, 2021.
* **Impacted Services:** Front-end services for other clusters in the region also made calls to the impacted cluster's front-end service to obtain configuration. These calls were timed out due to unavailability, triggering the same unhandled failure condition and resulting crash.

**Root Cause:**

The root cause of the outage was a code defect in a version update of a component that controls network traffic routing between Azure regions. The main parameters of the new code were invoked only at production scale and scope levels, which led to the prevention of anomaly detection from occurring. This resulted in an abnormal, sudden increase in the number of unhealthy devices and forced a health validation of those devices before removing routes from the network.

**Downtime Period:**

The downtime period was approximately 6 hours and 36 minutes.

**Resolution Time:**

The outage was marked as resolved by 03:26 UTC on February 26, 2021.

* Code Engine - Impacted customers experienced delays in creating or updating applications, due to the degraded performance of the system.

**Root Cause**

The third-party vendor's change to their BGP configuration caused a critical set of IP prefixes to be withdrawn, leading to the outage.

**Timeline of Events**

1. 21 June 2022 06:27 - The third-party vendor applied changes to their BGP configuration.
2. 21 June 2022 06:34 - IBM Cloud Specialists were alerted to HTTP 500 errors on their applications protected by Internet Services. Incident started.
3. 21 June 2022 06:44 - The third-party vendor notified IBM about a Global outage on their global PoPs.
4. 21 June 2022 07:42 - The third-party vendor reverted all changes.
5. 21 June 2022 08:06 - Customers and service teams reported restoration of services. Incident ended.

**Additional Information**

The incident was classified as a recurring event, but in this instance, it was not. The third-party vendor will make improvements to their change management procedure by 21 September 2022.

Outage Filename: ./20190823-Summary of the Amazon EC2 Issues in the Asia Pacific (Tokyo) Region (AP-NORTHEAST-1).txt
--
Based on the provided text, I will resume the outage for Amazon AWS.

**Outage Details:**

* **Cloud Provider:** Amazon AWS
* **Incident:** A small percentage of EC2 servers in a single Availability Zone (AZ) in the Tokyo (AP-NORTHEAST-1) Region shut down due to overheating.
* **Start Time:** 12:36 PM JST on August 23, 2019
* **Duration:** The outage lasted for approximately 3 hours and 45 minutes.

**Impacted Services and Regions/AZs:**

* Amazon EC2 in the Tokyo (AP-NORTHEAST-1) Region, specifically in a single Availability Zone.
* Amazon EBS resources in the affected area of the Availability Zone.
* Some other services, such as RDS, Redshift, ElastiCache, and Workspaces, would have seen some impact if their underlying EC2 instances were affected.

**Root Cause:**
The root cause of the outage was a control system failure that caused multiple, redundant cooling systems to fail in parts of the affected Availability Zone.

**Downtime Period:**

* The affected cooling systems were restored at 3:21 PM JST.
* Temperatures in the affected areas began to return to normal after the cooling systems were restored.
* Power was restored to the affected instances by 6:30 PM JST.
* A small number of instances and volumes hosted on hardware that was adversely affected by the loss of power and excessive heat took longer to recover.

**Resolved Time:** The outage was marked as resolved at 6:30 PM JST on August 23, 2019.
